entries.title: Proverbs 6:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Surety - Rashly, without considering how thou shalt discharge the debt as occasion require. Otherwise suretyship in some cases may be not only lawful, but an act of justice and charity. Stricken thy hand - Obliged thyself by giving thine hand, as the custom then was in such cases. With - With the creditor, whom he calls a stranger, because the usurers in Israel, who lent money to others, upon condition of paying use for it, were either Heathens, or were reputed as bad as Heathens, because this practice was forbidden by God's law, Deut 23:19.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hand - Into the power. Friend - Of the debtor, for whom, as being thy friend, thou didst become surety; whereby thou art in his power, by his neglect or unfaithfulness, to expose thee to the payment of the debt. Make sure - Or, and prevail with thy friend, strive to win him by thine incessant and earnest solicitations.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Give not sleep - Until thou hast taken care for the discharge of this obligation.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Travelleth - Swiftly and unexpectedly. Armed man - Irresistibly.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hate - Above many other sins which have a worse name in the world.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Deviseth - He whose practice it is to contrive wickedness. Swift - Such as greedily execute their wicked designs.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The law - The word of God, which thy parents delivered to thee.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bind them - Constantly remember, and duly consider them.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: It - The law of God which thy parents have taught thee. Talk - It shall give thee counsel and comfort.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Restore - He speaks not of that restitution which the law required, but of that which either the wronged person might force the thief to make, or which the thief would willingly give rather than be exposed to public shame.

entries.title: Proverbs 6:34
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rage - It enflames a man with rage. In the day - When he hath an opportunity to avenge himself.
